lines: GENESIS.
Iacob.
Iacob : I haue ſeiourned : and haue been with I aban vntil this preſeut
day. 5. I haue oxen, & aſſes, & ſheep, & men ſeruants: & woman ſer-
uants : & now I ſend a legacie to my Lord, that I may find grace in thy
ſight. 6. And the meſſengers returned to Iacob, ſaying: We came to Eſau
thy brother, & behold he compneth with ſpeed to meet thee with foute
hundred men, 7. Iacob teared exceedingly : and being ſore aftraid
diuided the people that was with him, the flockes alſo and the ſheep,
and the oxen, and the camels , into two troups, 8. ſaying : It Eſau
come to one troup, and ſtrike it the other troup that temaineth
ſhal be ſaued. 9. And Iacob ſaid : O God of my tather Abraham,
and God of my father Iſaac : O Lord that didleſt ſay to me: Re.
turne into thy land, and into the place of thy natiuitie, and I wil
doe thee good: 10. I am inferiour to al thy mercies, and thy truth
that thou haſt fulfilled to thy ſeruant. With my ſtaffe I paſſed ouer
this Iordan: aud now with two troupes I doe returne. 1. Deliuer
me from the hand of my brother Eſau, becauſe I am ſore affraid
of him: Ieſt perhaps he come, and ſtrike the mother with the chil-
dren. 12. Thou dideſt ſay that thou wouldeſt doe good to me, and
dilate my ſeed as the ſand of the ſea, which for multitude catr not
be numbred. 12. And when he had ſlept there that night, he ſe-
parated of thoſe things which he had, guifts to his brother
Eſau, 14. ſhe goats two hundred, he goats twentie, ewes
two hundred and ramines twentie, 15. thirtie milch camels
with their colts, fourtie kine, and twentie buls, twentie ſhe
aſſes, and theit toles ten. 16. And he ſent by the hands of his ſer-
uants euerie flock by it ſelfe, and he ſaid to his ſeruants: Goe
before me, and let there be a ſpace between flock and flock.
17. And he commanded the former, ſaying : If thou meet my bto-
ther Eſau, and he aske thee, whoſe art thou? or whither goeſt
thou? or whoſe are theſe that thou doeſt tollow? 18. thou ſhalt
anſwer : Iacobes thy ſetuant, he hath ſent them tor guifts to my
Lord Eſau: himſelfe alſo commeth after vs. 19. In like mannet he
gaue commandements to the ſecond, and the third, and to al that fol-
lowed the flocks, ſaying: With the ſelte- ſame words ſpeake ve to
Eſau, when vou ſhal find him. 20. And ye ſhal adde : Iacob alſo thy
Ieruant himſelfe followeth on aftet vs : for he ſaid : I wil pacifie him
with the guifts that goe before, and afterward I wil ſee him, perhaps
he wil be gracious vnto me. 21. The guifts therefore went betore him,
but himſelfe lodged that night in the campe. 22. And when he was riſen
carly , he tooke his two wiues, and his handmaids as manie, with his
eleuen ſonnes, and paſſed ouer the ford Iaboc. 23. And when he had
ſet ouer al things that appertained to him, 24. he taried alone: and be-
hold a man wraſtled with him til morning. 25. Who when he ſaw
that he could not ouercome him, he touched the ſinow of his thigh,
and torthwith it ſhranke. 26. And he ſaid to him : Let me goe tor it
